questions.question: Before driving downhill, you should:

options.text: Take your vehicle out of gear.
Shift into a lower gear.
Move into the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into a lower gear.
questions.explanation: Shift into a lower gear before going downhill. This helps you avoid overusing your brakes.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Drive on the shoulder.
Pull off the roadway.
Drive faster.
Allow the vehicle to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the vehicle to pass.
questions.explanation: Let the tailgating vehicle pass. Create more space in front of your vehicle. This helps you avoid sudden stops and reduces the risk of being hit from behind. Speeding up will only make things more dangerous.

questions.question: When inspecting the inside of a bus, you should:

options.text: Assume all emergency exits work properly.
Loosen every seat.
Check all signaling devices.
Not waste time looking at the handrails and floor lining.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check all signaling devices.
questions.explanation: Check that all signaling devices work properly, such as emergency bathroom buzzers. Make sure everything inside the bus is safe and in good working order.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:

options.text: Press the brake pedal down gradually.
Push the brake pedal down quickly.
Press the brake pedal repeatedly, but not hold it down continuously.
Use the same amount of brake pressure every time you slow or stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal down gradually.
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal smoothly and gradually every time you slow or stop. The amount of brake pressure you need depends on your speed and how quickly you need to stop.

questions.question: When coming to a stop, apply the brake pedal by:

options.text: Pushing down gradually.
Pushing down quickly.
Pulling up gradually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pushing down gradually.
questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down gradually when stopping. This helps you keep proper control of your vehicle.

questions.question: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under a bridge or sign, you should:

options.text: Drive faster.
Drive more slowly.
Drive on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive more slowly.
questions.explanation: Slow down and take a different route if possible. Do not risk hitting an overhead object.

questions.question: Black ice is:

options.text: Usually thick.
Usually thin.
Not a hazard when driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually thin.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it, so it looks like a wet road. Be alert for black ice when the road looks wet but the temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: A vehicle inspection:

options.text: Is a waste of time.
Helps catch small problems before they become big ones.
Should not be done by the driver.
Should be performed once a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps catch small problems before they become big ones.
questions.explanation: Inspect your vehicle before every trip. Finding a small problem before you drive is much better than discovering a major problem while driving.

questions.question: On long trips, you should stop and take a break ____ to avoid getting too tired.

options.text: Every half hour
Every hour
Every two hours
Every six hours

questions.correctAnswerText: Every two hours
questions.explanation: Stop for a break at least every two hours or after driving 100 miles. This reduces fatigue on long trips.

questions.question: When backing up, it is best to:

options.text: Rely only on the passenger's side mirror.
Back up quickly.
Turn toward the passenger's side whenever possible.
Use a helper, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a helper, if possible.
questions.explanation: Back up slowly and use both mirrors. Use a helper to watch for blind spots when possible. You and your helper should agree on a signal to stop.

questions.question: Federal and state laws require drivers to:

options.text: Inspect their vehicles regularly.
Inspect their vehicles only if they think there may be a problem.
Inspect their vehicles only when planning to travel out-of-state.
Inspect their vehicles only when carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inspect their vehicles regularly.
questions.explanation: Commercial drivers must inspect their vehicles before every trip. Regular inspections help drivers find problems early, before they become dangerous or expensive.

questions.question: After passengers board your bus, you should:

options.text: Start driving as soon as the door closes.
Warn passengers before you start driving.
Give passengers time to sit or hold on before you start driving.
Start driving as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give passengers time to sit or hold on before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Start and stop as smoothly as possible to prevent passenger injury. After passengers board, let them sit down or find something to hold onto before you begin driving.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, a bus driver should:

options.text: Stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest track.
Drive carefully but only stop if a train is crossing.
Speed up to get momentum to cross the tracks.
Roll up all the windows.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest track.
questions.explanation: Stop 15 to 50 feet before any railroad crossing. Check for trains before crossing the tracks. You can open the door to help you see or hear an approaching train.

questions.question: When near a railroad crossing:

options.text: You will hear every approaching train.
You may not hear a train, even if one is coming.
You will hear two short horn blasts if a train is approaching.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not hear a train, even if one is coming.
questions.explanation: Never assume you will hear an approaching train. The train operator may not sound the horn, or horns may be prohibited in some areas. Noise inside your vehicle may also prevent you from hearing a train until it is very close.

questions.question: Carry-on bags should be placed:

options.text: In front of the back door.
In front of the front door.
Where they do not block any emergency exits.
On top of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where they do not block any emergency exits.
questions.explanation: Do not leave bags in doorways or aisles. Secure all items so passengers can exit through any door or window in an emergency.

questions.question: Skids caused by speeding up can usually be fixed by:

options.text: Speeding up more.
Taking your foot off the accelerator.
Coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking your foot off the accelerator.
questions.explanation: Skids from speeding up happen often on slippery roads. You can usually fix these skids by taking your foot off the accelerator.

questions.question: Looking far ahead while driving is:

options.text: Not helpful because there is little you can do about things far ahead.
Good practice to spot dangers early.
Not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Good practice to spot dangers early.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to spot dangers early and respond safely.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will:

options.text: Explain what you know about the inspection process.
Watch someone else inspect your vehicle.
Watch a film about vehicle inspection.
Change all the tires on your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you know about the inspection process.
questions.explanation: You will do a complete inspection of your vehicle. You must explain what you are checking and why.

questions.question: When inspecting your vehicle, which of these should NOT worry you?

options.text: Exhaust parts rubbing against fuel system parts
Exhaust parts that are leaking
Missing mounting brackets
Exhaust parts made of aluminum

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust parts made of aluminum
questions.explanation: Check for loose, broken, or missing exhaust pipes, mufflers, or tailpipes. Look for loose or missing brackets, clamps, bolts, or nuts. Watch for exhaust parts rubbing against fuel system parts or other moving parts. Check for leaks in exhaust parts.

questions.question: When driving, you should:

options.text: Always drive at the posted speed limit.
Always drive slightly below the posted speed limit.
Change your speed based on road and traffic conditions.
Drive as fast as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your speed based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast causes many fatal crashes. Always adjust your speed to match current road and traffic conditions.
